messages:
anya: FYI model-router p95 latency alert started firing around 01:48 UTC. It looks correlated with the nightly batch job that kicks off at ~01:45. Dashboard: https://grafana.company/redwood/model-router -> panel 'latency.p95'. Can we do a short soft-snooze or bump threshold overnight?

chris: Can you paste the query or a link to the exact alert rule? I want to double-check if it's the same rule we tweaked last month.

anya: Alert rule link: https://alerts.company/rules/5687. Query uses prometheus: max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, job))[10m:]) > 1200.

mike: Is the traffic coming from the async batch worker or user-facing? If it's purely the batch window we can add a schedule-based suppression (02:00-03:30 UTC) for 3 nights.

anya: Looks like batch-worker-2 and batch-worker-3 tasks have most of the spikes. Traces show long tail due to bulk KV lookups. Sample span: ```trace_id=abc123 service=model-router span=kv_fetch duration_ms=1800 tags={batch=true}```

jun: +1 to temporary suppression. We should avoid changing long-term threshold because user SLOs still matter outside that window. Proposal: add 90m suppression starting 01:30 UTC tonight and auto-expire after 3 occurrences.

chris: OK. Quick question — where should we document this decision so oncall knows why alerts were muted? Runbook? Ops-incident notes?

mike: I'll add a short entry in the 'model-router' runbook under "temporary alert suppressions" and include the Grafana snapshot + trace link. Also will open a PR to add scheduled suppression in our alerting repo: https://git.company/alerts/merge_requests -> will tag @jun for review.

anya: Thanks. Can someone actually flip the suppression for tonight? I'm heads-down on the batch job fix.

sre-bot: Incident suppression created by mike — rule 5687 suppressed from 1923460200 to 1923465600 (90m). Reason: nightly batch KV tailing causes p95 spikes. Link: https://alerts.company/suppressions/7890

jun: Thanks mike and sre-bot. Can we also add a note to the PR to revisit threshold after two successful nights? If spikes persist we'll need a mitigation in the router (KV caching or parallelization).

mike: Yep will add that to the PR description. Scheduling the PR and the runbook update now. ETA ~ 30m.

anya: Perfect. I'll monitor tonight and post an update in the morning. :thumbsup:

chris: Thanks all. If anyone sees unexpected user impact, ping me directly.
